bug_description: An undefined-behavior left shift occurs in ares_calc_query_timeout() (src/lib/ares_process.c:1156) in c-ares when a DNS query is requeued 64 or more times for a single server. The expression timeplus <<= rounds uses an unbounded shift exponent computed from query->try_count / num_servers. With a single configured server and repeated connection failures, rounds grows without bound, eventually reaching 64 which exceeds the width of the 64-bit size_t type and invokes undefined behavior per the C standard. The existing channel->maxtimeout cap runs after the offending shift expression and cannot prevent the UB.
build_sh:
#!/bin/bash -eu
set -eu
cd /src/c-ares

# Build c-ares as a static library using cmake
mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake .. \
    -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$CC" \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="$CFLAGS" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCARES_STATIC=ON \
    -DCARES_SHARED=OFF \
    -DCARES_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF \
    -DCARES_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
    -DCARES_BUILD_CONTAINER_TESTS=OFF
make -j$(nproc)

# Find the static library
LIBCARES=$(find /src/c-ares/build -name 'libcares.a' | head -1)
if [ -z "$LIBCARES" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: libcares.a not found"
    exit 1
fi

# Compile harness against the static library
cd /src
$CC $CFLAGS \
    -I /src/c-ares/include \
    -I /src/c-ares/build \
    /src/harness.c \
    "$LIBCARES" \
    -o /src/harness_bin \
    -lpthread
secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR c-ares.issue-1144..."
    UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1 /src/harness_bin
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/c-ares
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

bug_report:
================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/c-ares/c-ares/issues/1144
## Description:
Issue: c-ares/c-ares#1144
Title: Shift Exponent Too Large in ares_calc_query_timeout via Repeated Connection Failure
State: open
Created at: 2026-04-21

Issue Body:
An undefined-behavior (UB) left shift occurs in `ares_calc_query_timeout()` when a query is requeued 64 or more times per configured server. The expression `timeplus <<= rounds` is never bounded before the shift, so when `rounds >= 64`, the shift exponent exceeds the width of the 64-bit `size_t` type, invoking undefined behavior per the C standard.

The variable `rounds` is computed as `query->try_count / num_servers`. Each failed connection attempt increments `try_count` via the async requeue path. With a single configured server (`num_servers == 1`), `rounds` equals `try_count` directly. After 64 connection failures, the expression `timeplus <<= 64` is executed, which is UB. The existing `channel->maxtimeout` cap runs after the offending shift expression and therefore cannot prevent the UB.

The failures arrive asynchronously through the event loop (not via synchronous recursion), so `try_count` simply grows one iteration at a time until it crosses the 64-bit shift threshold.

**Location:** src/lib/ares_process.c, function ares_calc_query_timeout(), line 1156

**Reproduction:** Configure c-ares with a single non-responsive DNS server (e.g. 127.0.0.1:53 with nothing listening), set opts.tries to a high value (>= 65), set opts.timeout and opts.maxtimeout to 1ms, and run a DNS query. After 64 connection failures and requeues, the shift UB fires.

**Vulnerable version:** v1.31.0-332-g46b7f689
